titulo: Kernel prepatch 7.4-rc2
resumo: Linus Torvalds has released the 7.4-rc2 prepatch and it will come as no surprise that it is a large one (" a big -rc2 to go with the largest ever -rc1 "). Much of the size was made up of some automated Coccinelle updates that were spread out all over the tree; once those are factored out, the rest looks fairly normal: When masking that noise out from the diffstat, the shape of it changes - not spread out over thousands of files any more. But it does not look unusual: a third is drivers (gpu, networking and sound account for most of it, but there's a bit of everything), another third is networking and bpf, and the final third is "the rest" (mostly filesystems, mm, arch updates). And yes, much of this was driven by various AI fixes. I think I'll stop repeating that, and we can just take it for granted. But this time around Alexei [Starovoitov] claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true.

O vilão da história é o processo atieclxx.exe (vinculado ao AMD External Events Utility), serviço responsável por gerenciar atalhos do aplicativo e detecção de monitores. Em sistemas afetados, esse processo mantém uma taxa constante de escrita que varia entre 0,3 MB/s e 1,5 MB/s, com casos mais graves atingindo até 5 MB/s sustentados . titulo: Can Agentic Robotics Solve Robotics’ Data Scaling Problem?
resumo: Robotics companies are investing heavily in the belief that data will solve the most difficult problems in robotics. Once AI systems have ingested enough data from human demonstrations, the thinking goes, robots will be able to perform the vast majority of the manual tasks that humans now do. There are even robotics companies that exist solely to collect training data and sell it to other robotics companies in pursuit of this goal. But whether data will finally bring us general-purpose robots is an open question . Nobody knows how much data would be necessary , what kind of data is important , or whether something else might be missing . And there are other problems with a reliance on massive amounts of data: the resulting AI algorithms are essentially black boxes, which despite their high performance are difficult or impossible for humans to understand. This characteristic is becoming increasingly concerning in commercial deployments, where robots must be flexible, reliable, and safe. At the 2026 Conference on Robot Learning this week, UC Berkeley and NVIDIA are jointly announcing a new approach to using AI to program robots for everyday practical tasks in industrial environments.

titulo: Sharing a Windows PC? Why you should disable EFS before it’s too late
resumo: Windows’ Encrypted File System (EFS for short) is showing its age. Although it’s still very easy to use – just right-click on a file or folder and select Properties > Advanced > Encrypt contents to protect data – the risk of losing the decryption key is still pretty high. Unlike BitLocker, which encrypts an entire drive, EFS is designed to protect individual files and folders. This can be useful in some situations, but it also means that users may not always be aware of which data they have encrypted. That’s why most folks switched to alternatives like BitLocker, which comes with Windows, or VeraCrypt . The danger with using EFS is that you might encrypt important data, then delete your account and forget to backup the key beforehand. Unfortunately, there’s no way to decrypt data again after that. Especially on company PCs or computers used by multiple people. That’s why we recommend you disable the use of EFS. It reduces the risk of inadvertently encrypting files that could become inaccessible later. Before doing that though, you should check if your files are already encrypted.
